correctness.rationale: After reducing to the block functional calculus in \(B=|A^*|\), the spectral theorem makes the operator fibrewise equal to \(M_t\). Equality in the global norm bound occurs exactly when a nonzero vector is supported on the maximizing set \(\Omega\) and lies in the fibrewise top singular subspace. This is possible exactly when \(E_B(\Omega)\ne0\). The singleton case reduces to an eigenvalue, and the explicit multiplication-operator example satisfies the formula symbolically.

value.rationale: The maximizing set \(\Omega\) is intrinsic to the focal paper's norm formula. Replacing a singleton/eigenvalue condition by the exact spectral-mass criterion completes the natural norm-attainment classification for the whole structured family, including a genuinely non-atomic regime in which the block operator attains its norm while \(A\) does not.
